_why: 🔴 THIS FILE CARRIES NO `purchasable` BOOLEAN, AND IT NEVER MAY.
Whether the bundle can be bought is DERIVED — tooling/bundle-availability.mjs computes it
from the registers that already exist, and tooling/ci/assert-bundle-availability.mjs fails
the build if a boolean literal ever appears here or if the derivation stops deriving.
A flag in this file would be a coming-soon gate that any stray edit could flip open, on the
one surface where being wrong means advertising a subscription that cannot be delivered.
As of 2026-09-09 the derivation answers FALSE, from data: catalog/apps.json has ONE `live`
row (subscriptiontracker) and extensions/catalog/extensions.json has ONE `preview` row
(fullshot), so the live-product count is 1 and 1 >= 2 is false. Flipping fullshot's `status`
to `live` in its own catalogue is the whole enable trigger — nothing else changes.
⚠️ NO PRICE AMOUNTS HERE, ONLY PRICE IDS. [pipeline 5]M-11 — a displayed price comes from
the rail, never from a file in this repo. `priceIds` are opaque rail handles; the amount
they resolve to is the rail's answer and is fetched, not stored.
⚠️ THIS IS THE DRAFT DEFINITION, NOT A MINTED VERSION. `feature_sets` /
`feature_set_members` in platform_db are the PINNED record a grant points at ([ADR 057] §4),
and minting a version into them is a dated, reviewed act. Editing this file changes what a
FUTURE grant would be sold under; it can never change what an existing grant already owns.
⚠️ `storeProducts` IS EMPTY UNTIL OWNER STEP O-D3 CREATES THE STORE SKUs. Each entry is
{app, store, plan, productId, term}: the app whose store listing sells the bundle (an Apple
product id belongs to one app), the rail (apple-iap | play-billing), the plan (bundle-monthly |
bundle-yearly — a lifetime is never sold in-app), the id read back from the store console, and
the term (`subscription`: every in-app plan is one, so the grant rolls to the current sellable
version; render refuses `one_time`). tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs renders them into services/platform/src/lib/mor/store-skus.ts,
where the RevenueCat route tells a bundle SKU from a single-app one. An id typed here before the
store holds it would route a purchase of nothing.
name: Nikatru bundle

paddle._why: EMPTY UNTIL THE OFFER EXISTS. A price id is minted in the rail's dashboard against a real product; inventing one here would make the derivation's price limb pass over a handle that resolves to nothing, and the first buyer would meet a 404 at checkout. Empty is the honest state and the derivation reads it as NOT purchasable.
